heuristicSample.titleEn: Centre Back — Basic Ball Shift vs 6:0
heuristicSample.questionEn: What is your first job before forcing a shot?
heuristicSample.optimalEn: Shift the ball once to move the block, then attack the gap or feed
heuristicSample.goodEn: Threaten a drive first to freeze the centre, then shift the ball
notes: optimal and good both plausible system answers — thin single-best cue

heuristicSample.titleEn: Centre Back — Tempo When Protecting a Lead
heuristicSample.questionEn: How do you set tempo while still threatening to score?
heuristicSample.optimalEn: Structured build-up, use the clock, attack only on clear gaps
heuristicSample.goodEn: One quick attack if a clear break opens, otherwise rebuild
notes: optimal and good both plausible system answers — thin single-best cue

heuristicSample.questionEn: What is your first responsibility in this break?
heuristicSample.optimalEn: Delay centrally and direct wing coverage with clear communication
heuristicSample.goodEn: Sprint to cut the far-wing skip first, then recover to the middle
notes: cartoon/weak distractor (poor): Stop to protest the turnover before recovering goal-side

heuristicSample.questionEn: What is the right final-possession standard here?
heuristicSample.optimalEn: Take the best available system shot before the clock expires
heuristicSample.goodEn: One decisive pass to the open back, then they finish inside the clock
notes: optimal and good both plausible system answers — thin single-best cue

heuristicSample.titleEn: Centre Back — Calm Direction When Trailing
heuristicSample.questionEn: How do you lead the next attack without turning it into panic?
heuristicSample.optimalEn: Stay calm, call one clear structure, take calculated risks inside it
heuristicSample.goodEn: Speed up ball movement inside the same structure to create earlier gaps
notes: optimal and good both plausible system answers — thin single-best cue

qualitativeSample.titleEn: Centre Back — Basic Ball Shift vs 6:0
qualitativeSample.issue: Optimal ("Shift the ball once…") and good ("Threaten a drive first… then shift") are both correct CB habits; situation lacks a cue that uniquely ranks one above the other.

qualitativeSample.titleEn: Centre Back — Building the Pivot Connection
qualitativeSample.issue: Good ("Shoot if the fake makes both half-backs drop") can be equally correct when the cue is only "narrow lane into the seal"; no half-step timing cue forces pass-first.

qualitativeSample.titleEn: Centre Back — Tempo When Protecting a Lead
qualitativeSample.issue: Optimal and good are both tempo-control coaching advice; "clear gaps" vs "clear break" are nearly interchangeable without a concrete read.
Optimal (take best system shot) vs good (one decisive pass then finish) are both correct final-possession standards; situation says both a playable gap AND eight seconds — either can be right.

qualitativeSample.titleEn: Centre Back — Calm Direction When Trailing
qualitativeSample.issue: Optimal is a pure coaching platitude ("Stay calm, call one clear structure…") with no tactical cue; good is a more specific tempo choice and may be stronger.
Poor ("Stop to protest the turnover…") is a cartoon distractor; optimal vs good (delay centre vs cut far-wing skip) both viable without a clearer first-threat cue.

coverageNotes.5v6: False positive risk: "short-handed defender" in 6-on-5 family. Corrected regex treats true 5v6 as missing.
coverageNotes.open/individual: Earlier "otvoren" hits were "otvorene strane" (open side), not open/individual defence. Corrected to missing.
coverageNotes.passive: Earlier hits were "pasivna držanja" / "passive holds" in poor-answer feedback, not the passive-play rule. Corrected to missing.
coverageNotes.gk_reading: Tightened away from generic "blok/block" (screens). Remaining hits require GK/vratar language.
